title: useNavigate
summary: Navigate to a URL or move through browser history.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: The hook takes no arguments. The returned NavigateFunction accepts a string URL, a number of history entries, or an object with pathname, search, and hash. Its optional second argument contains NavigateOptions.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: Returns a stable callback for the current router. The callback returns void, including for URL navigation. If you need to await navigation, call useRouter().navigate instead.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: The object form retains omitted URL parts. Set search or hash to an empty string when you want to remove them.

sections.title: History and deployments
sections.body: A numeric target calls window.history.go and is browser-only. URL targets go through the router and its installed navigation integrations. Use mountApplication when you need browser history state, retained views, and deployment handoff behavior; a bare provider does not install all those integrations. For ordinary navigable content, prefer Link so users retain anchor interactions.
